items.independentDerivation: The denominator vanishes at x=±1; f tends to 0 at both infinite ends, f(0)=-1 and the numerator is never zero. For admissible nonzero x, f(x)=f(-x). On x>1 the function is strictly decreasing, so it is one-to-one.

items.independentDerivation: The three branches have ranges (-∞,-1], (1,4] and (13,∞), respectively. They are disjoint and each branch is increasing, so f is injective and the inverse domain is their union.

items.independentDerivation: The contrapositive of x₁≠x₂ implies f(x₁)≠f(x₂) is f(x₁)=f(x₂) implies x₁=x₂. For 3x+4, equality of outputs gives 3x₁+4=3x₂+4 and hence x₁=x₂ for all real inputs.
items.reasoningRationale: Recognises an equivalent logical statement and applies it to a short, scaffolded linear proof.
holds: Separate paper-policy publication hold: James Ruse Y12 X2 2022.

items.independentDerivation: Both graphs meet the axes at (4,0) and (0,2). The root requires x≤4, so setting u=√(4-x)≥0 makes the strict inequality u>u²/2, giving 0<u<2 and 0<x<4. Swapping variables gives the inverse 4-x² on x≥0, with intercepts (0,4) and (2,0).
items.reasoningRationale: Links graph comparison and a root–modulus inequality with the familiar inverse procedure; the parts provide substantial structure.
holds: Separate paper-policy publication hold: Normanhurst Y11 X1 2019.

items.taughtMethodFit: Self-inverse is defined in the task; applying inverse composition and domain–range exchange to a parameterised reciprocal is a suitable transfer of taught methods.
items.uniqueWholeDemand: Determining when a parameterised restricted reciprocal is self-inverse, including equality of its domain and range, is distinct from the supplied accepted tasks.
items.independentDerivation: Write f(x)=2+(a+4)/(x-2). At a=-4 it is constant and has no inverse function. For a≠-4 the reciprocal rule is formally involutive. Its range is (2,∞) when a>-4 and (-∞,2) when a<-4. Only a>-4 makes the range equal to the given domain, and then composition is defined throughout that domain and equals x.
items.reasoningRationale: Requires connecting a parameterised involutive rule with its restricted domain and range; formal algebra alone does not settle the function question.
corrections: Restore the substantive graphical alternative with an editable graph or equivalent explanation: compare the right-hand branch with its reflection in y=x and explain why a>-4 preserves the given domain. Correct the source's overbroad claim that self-inverse functions must lie in the same quadrant.
Qualify the displayed composition for a<-4 as a formal rule calculation: f(x)<2 then lies outside the stated domain, so f(f(x)) is not defined as a composition of the restricted function.

items.independentDerivation: For x>2, f has range (-5,∞), so the inverse has domain x>-5 and range (2,∞); solving gives f⁻¹(x)=2+3/(x+5). The zero occurs at x=13/5. Reflecting the negative portion above the axis gives |f| a minimum there, vertical asymptote x=2 and horizontal asymptote y=5. Values between 0 and 5 occur twice, so |f| is not one-to-one.
